title: Nernst equation (qualitative use)

items.label: E
items.meaning: cell potential under the actual (nonstandard) conditions (volts)

items.label: E^{\circ}
items.meaning: standard cell potential, which corresponds to Q = 1 (volts)

items.label: n
items.meaning: moles of electrons transferred in the redox reaction

items.label: F
items.meaning: Faraday constant (charge per mole of electrons)

items.label: Q
items.meaning: reaction quotient for the cell reaction

caution: Use it qualitatively: algorithmic Nernst calculations alone are insufficient. Justify with concentration effects and distance from equilibrium (|E| shrinks to zero as Q approaches K). Do not apply Le Châtelier's principle to the cell.
ced_evidence: 9.10.A.4 "the qualitative use of the Nernst equation: E = Eo − (RT/nF) ln Q"

title: Current and charge
caution: Time must be in seconds when current is in amperes and charge is in coulombs.

title: Standard entropy change of a reaction

items.label: \Delta S^{\circ}_{reaction}
items.meaning: standard entropy change for the process

items.label: \Sigma
items.meaning: sum over all species on that side of the equation

items.label: S^{\circ}_{products}
items.meaning: absolute (standard molar) entropies of the products

items.label: S^{\circ}_{reactants}
items.meaning: absolute (standard molar) entropies of the reactants

caution: Each S° is scaled by its stoichiometric coefficient before summing. Products minus reactants.

title: Gibbs free energy equation

items.label: \Delta G^{\circ}
items.meaning: standard Gibbs free energy change; below 0 means thermodynamically favored

caution: Use consistent energy units for ΔH° and TΔS°. When arguing favorability, reason from the signs of ΔH° and ΔS° and say which term drives the process; do not claim both help unless both signs support it.

title: ΔG° from standard free energies of formation

items.label: \Delta G^{\circ}_{reaction}
items.meaning: standard Gibbs free energy change for the process

items.label: \Sigma
items.meaning: sum over all species on that side of the equation

items.label: \Delta G_f^{\circ}{}_{products}
items.meaning: standard Gibbs free energies of formation of the products

items.label: \Delta G_f^{\circ}{}_{reactants}
items.meaning: standard Gibbs free energies of formation of the reactants

caution: Each ΔGf° is scaled by its stoichiometric coefficient. Products minus reactants. Applies to standard-state conditions.

title: Equilibrium constant from ΔG°
caution: ΔG° and RT must be in the same energy units. ΔG° < 0 gives K > 1 and ΔG° > 0 gives K < 1. When ΔG° is near zero, K is close to 1.

title: ΔG° from the equilibrium constant
caution: The sign is negative: K > 1 corresponds to ΔG° < 0 (products favored at equilibrium under standard conditions).

title: Free energy and standard cell potential

items.label: \Delta G^{\circ}
items.meaning: standard Gibbs free energy change of the cell reaction

items.label: n
items.meaning: moles of electrons transferred in the redox reaction

items.label: F
items.meaning: Faraday constant (charge per mole of electrons)

caution: ΔG° is proportional to the negative of E°. Positive E° means thermodynamically favored (galvanic) and negative E° means unfavored (needs an applied potential). Keep the units of F and E° consistent with ΔG°.
